title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache & parallelism
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Split CI into smaller workflows (lint, unit-test, integration, release) to improve parallelism and cache hit rates. Upgraded select GitHub Actions to latest stable, consolidated caching keys, and added targeted warm-up step for large matrix jobs. No runtime or API changes. Improvements should reduce average CI time for PRs by ~30% and improve reliability for release automation.
description: Motivation: Our monolithic CI workflow has become slow and brittle as we added more checks. This PR splits lint, unit tests, integration tests and release automation into dedicated workflows, consolidates cache keys, and tunes matrix parallelism to reduce queueing and improve cache hit rates. Goals: 1) Reduce average PR CI latency, 2) Improve cache effectiveness across the repo matrix, 3) Make release automation more robust and auditable. Changes: - Split .github/workflows/ci.yml into: .github/workflows/lint.yml, test-unit.yml, test-integration.yml, release.yml - Introduced a small cache warm-up job that primes large node_modules/bazel caches on dedicated runners to increase subsequent job cache hits - Upgraded actions/setup-node, actions/cache, and semantic-release actions to latest stable versions and pinned major versions where appropriate - Consolidated caching keys to separate dependency caches (node, python) from build artifacts and made keys more deterministic per package path - Reduced the default matrix concurrency on heavy integration jobs and added a lightweight smoke test job to fail-fast on obvious regressions - Added descriptive workflow run names and tagging so the Console and release automation can route flaky jobs differently Compatibility & rollout: This is a non-breaking CI-only change. We rolled out in canary by enabling lint.yml and test-unit.yml first for feature/* branches for 48 hours and monitored cache hit rates and run times. Observed a median CI wall-clock reduction of ~28% and cache hit rate increase of ~12% for node packages. Checklist: - [x] Split workflows and basic smoke tests - [x] Upgrade key actions and pin versions - [x] Add cache warm-up and deterministic cache keys - [x] Validate on canary branches for 48h - [x] Address reviewer feedback and flaky integration tests - [x] Merge with squash+merge Related: Linear ENG-1724 (ci split + perf tuning), ENG-1730 (release automation hygiene), SUP-412 (support ticket for flaky release job).

review_comments: Noah Patel: Nice split — can we make the cache keys include the package path to avoid cross-package invalidation?
Ava Martinez: Good point, updated cache keys to include package path and added tools/ci/cache-keys.md documenting the pattern.
Lina Chen: Integration matrix still consumes too many runners during peak. Suggest lowering parallelism for heavy infra tests.
Ava Martinez: Reduced concurrency for integration matrix from 8 -> 3 for non-dedicated branches; added a smoke job to catch quick failures earlier.
Marcus Reynolds: Release workflow looks good but add an explicit artifact upload before semantic-release to aid debugging.
Ava Martinez: Added artifact upload step and a small retry wrapper around the semantic-release job; also pinned semantic-release to v20.x.
Lina Chen: CI run showed a flaky integration test causing a single run failure; added a retry decorator to that test and filed ENG-1745 to investigate root cause.
Ava Martinez: Filed ENG-1745 and added a short-term retry on the failing test with comment referencing the Linear ticket.
